title: Indiana shakes off USC to near Playoff berth as Lincoln Riley’s Trojans stumble in must-win
content:
BLOOMINGTON, Ind. — Reigning national champion Indiana should be defending national champion Indiana in a few weeks, thanks to another game in which the Hoosiers had offense in fits and starts, quarterback inconsistencies and clutch plays late.

No. 9 Indiana has a 98 percent chance of being in the 12-team Playoff, per The Athletic’s Austin Mock, after Saturday’s 27-13 win over No. 18 USC at IU’s Memorial Stadium. The Hoosiers are 9-1, 6-1 in the Big Ten with Washington and Purdue left in the regular season. This triumph over the Trojans (7-3, 4-3) is Indiana’s best of the season and might stand as its lone ranked win in the end.

It also means Indiana vs. No. 4 UCLA (10-0, 7-0) is the most likely matchup in the final Big Ten championship game. But a loss there shouldn’t penalize the Hoosiers, given the quality of UCLA’s season and presuming a competitive game.

IU’s defense virtually guarantees that. It held down an explosive USC offense that put 30 on Ohio State its last time out, leaving the Trojans with slim Playoff hopes. IU’s offense raises questions about Curt Cignetti’s team making another December-and-January run. But it did have its moments Saturday.

Seventh-year senior Grant Wilson started at quarterback again, though Josh Hoover (arm) was available. Wilson made some spectacular throws, let USC back in the game with a pick late in the first half, put several other passes in harm’s way, but ultimately did enough to win. His 42-yard scoring loft to Charlie Becker with 3:30 left was a fitting mic drop for the Hoosiers and left Wilson with 305 yards passing and two touchdowns.

USC quarterback Jayden Maiava had his own moments and got cooking in the fourth quarter, completing four passes for 81 yards on a drive that reached the Indiana 8 and threatened to tie the score. But then Maiava telegraphed an ill-advised pass, intercepted by Isaiah Jones at the 1 with 6:35 to play, and he threw three picks for the day.

That was a familiar failure for a USC offense that came into the game 95th nationally in red zone scoring percentage (81.82 percent) and 61st in touchdown percentage (63.64 percent). Indiana’s defense came in 17th in opponent red zone scoring percentage (75 percent) and third in touchdown percentage (35 percent). The better unit prevailed when it mattered most.

It’s been a full decade since USC went on the road and beat a ranked team outside of Southern California.

You have to go all the way back to a win at No. 4 Washington in November 2016 — Clay Helton’s first season at head coach, with Sam Darnold at quarterback — for a ranked road win away from Greater Los Angeles. The Trojans only other ranked win away from The Coliseum since then was in 2022 over UCLA, which was also the first and only ranked road win of Lincoln Riley’s tenure.

On the heels of a win against Ohio State (albeit without quarterback Julian Sayin), USC had a chance for back-to-back resume-boosting victories that could have changed the tenor of this season and Riley’s job security. A win would have nudged USC into the CFP discussion and a logjam for second place in the Big Ten standings. Instead, Saturday was a familiar result, with USC getting bullied too often on the line of scrimmage, committing dumb penalties, and folding in high-pressure moments.

Riley and USC keep insisting this program is up to the task of competing in the Big Ten and for national championships. The results continue to suggest otherwise. — Justin Williams

TCU transfer and previous starter Josh Hoover, who has battled an arm injury, was active and not listed on the availability report. That presumably meant his return to the starting lineup. Curt Cignetti did not commit to that — but Cignetti did have Hoover on his radio show this week! Then he started seventh-year senior Grant Wilson. The former Old Dominion and Fordham quarterback, who made huge plays late to lead an Oct. 31 comeback win over Minnesota, was all over the map.

He let USC back in the game with a brutal pick late in the first half. He made spectacular throws, including a 65-yard post to Nick Marsh that couldn’t have been placed better. He had some head-scratching decisions and misfires. USC dropped several possible interceptions. Still, Wilson ended up with the win and 305 yards on 17-for-27 passing. — Joe Rexrode

Four dropped interceptions — including three in the end zone, and two on the same drive. A pair of completely unnecessary penalties on special teams. Two missed field goals, one a chip shot from 27 yards out. And a killer fourth-quarter interception by Maiava in the red zone while driving for the tying score. USC made it inside Indiana’s 35-yard line six times and had only one touchdown to show for it.

It’s actually a wonder the Trojans hung around as long as they did considering how many missteps they made along the way. It’s a big part of what makes the Riley era so frustrating. The talent is there. Resources, too. But the execution is consistently lacking. Call it soft or undisciplined or a West Coast program trying to hang in the bareknuckled Big Ten. However you want to label it, it’s not good enough from USC. — Williams

It looked as if the game was careening away from USC late in the second quarter, as the Trojans gifted Indiana points off a bad interception by Maiava and great field position off a couple of dumb penalties. But then a tipped pass by Wilson fell into the hands of USC’s Deven Bryant in the final minute of the first half, followed immediately by a 51-yard pass from Maiava to Kayden Dixon-Wyatt. That set up a 7-yard touchdown strike from Maiava to Zacharyus Williams with 21 seconds on the clock. Instead of Indiana going up two scores and getting the ball to start the second half, USC knotted the score at 10 and completely shifted the vibe entering halftime. — Williams

The Hoosiers came into Saturday’s game with a slumping rushing attack — among the nation’s best early in the season against a lighter schedule, but averaging just 103.3 yards in the previous four games. Late in the third quarter Saturday, IU had managed just 54 yards on 21 carries.

But then Khobie Martin took a toss sweep to the boundary, followed a caravan of blockers and ended up just shy of the end zone on a 37-yard sprint. Martin finished it off on the next play.

Martin missed six games with an arm injury before returning in the Oct. 31 win over Minnesota and getting 7 yards on three carries. He had 82 of IU’s 146 yards rushing on 12 carries against USC and could form a nice tandem with Lee Beebe Jr. (16 carries, 71 yards) down the stretch.

This story will be updated.
